chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥadīd, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj and others, from one of the two Imams عليهما السلام, concerning:
A man who reverted from Islam—he said: “He is to be asked to repent; if he repents, otherwise he is killed.”
It was said to Jamīl: What do you say if he repents and then again reverts from Islam? He said: “He is to be asked to repent.”

Then it was said: What do you say if he repents, then reverts, then repents, then reverts? He said: “I have not heard anything about this, but in my view he is in the position of the fornicator upon whom the legal punishment is carried out twice, then after that he is killed.”

key_terms.الزَّانِي: the fornicator, used here in legal analogy
key_terms.الْإِسْلَامِ: Islam, the religion from which the person turned back
key_terms.رَجَعَ: reverted or turned back, here meaning apostatized from Islam
key_terms.قُتِلَ: he was killed, referring to the legal punishment
key_terms.يُسْتَتَابُ: he is asked to repent and return

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith in Tahdhib al-Ahkam say about repeated apostasy and repentance?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a man who apostasizes from Islam, stating that he is asked to repent and, if he repents, he is spared; otherwise, he is executed. It also records a further question to Jamīl ibn Darrāj about repeated apostasy, where he reports no direct transmitted ruling but offers an analogy to the repeated punishment of a fornicator.
